newsitem.title: USA: Texfi to close some operations, take charge.
newsitem.headline: Texfi to close some operations, take charge.

text.p: Texfi Industries Inc said Friday it will discontinue its commodity T-shirt knitting and sewing operations in Haw River, N.C., and Olanta, S.C., respectively; consolidate its narrow fabric operations into its Asheboro N.C., facility; and close its Graham, N.C., facility.
The company said the discontinuance and consolidation will result in a one-time charge of about $14 million to be taken in the fourth quarter of the company's 1996 fiscal year, which ends today.
Of the $14 million to be charged off, $3 million is expected to be in cash.

The company said it anticipates that as assets of the closed facilities are sold and inventories and receivables are liquidated, it will be able to reduce its debt by at least $20 million and reduce future interest costs in excess of $1.5 million annually.
The company said it will continue to market sports apparel and private label fashion tops under its newly-formed Kingstree Marketing organization.

The company said the discontinuation of the commodity T-shirt business and consolidation of the Graham facility, while resulting in a one-time charge, will enable the company to exit operations which are anticipated to account for $50 million in sales, but will have generated operating losses of about $7 million in FY96.
Dane Vincent, Texfi's chief financial officer, said the realignment will result in laying off 484 employees.
"This is an effort to focus on the strength of our company," Vincent said. "The production of synthetic products is where our strength is."
